index.downloadDescription: Export the full glossary as an Excel or CSV file. Either can be re-uploaded on the import and replace pages.
index.importDescription: Upload a CSV file to bulk-import glossary entries. The file must match the downloaded format.
index.importHint: Upload a CSV, review entries side-by-side, and import in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms.
index.replaceDescription: Upload a CSV file to completely replace the glossary. Every existing entry is deleted first, so download a backup before you start.
index.replaceHint: Upload a CSV to discard the current glossary and replace it with the file's entries.

chunked.author: Author: {{author}}

columns.uuidImport: optional; links a row to an existing database entry (use the downloaded export to preserve IDs)
columns.uuidReplace: optional; groups rows into one entry and preserves the entry's ID
columns.englishTermImport: English translation; rows without this field are used only for metadata updates
columns.englishTermReplace: English translation; rows without this field contribute metadata only
columns.phonetic: pronunciation guide (applies to the whole entry)
columns.author: translation author (applies to the whole entry)
columns.chineseSutraText: Chinese context sentence for the translation
columns.englishSutraText: English context sentence for the translation

chunked.stepUpload: Upload — select your CSV or XLSX file and click Preview. Both file types are parsed locally in your browser — no file data is sent to the server, so large files are handled without hitting upload size limits.
chunked.stepRepeat: Repeat until all chunks are {{done}}. The progress bar at the top tracks how far along you are.

import.title: Import Glossary
import.description: Upload a CSV or XLSX file to review and import glossary entries in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms at a time.
import.reviewing: Reviewing {{terms}} ({{rows}}). Upload a new file above to start over.
import.inspectDescription: The Glossary Inspector shows every entry with its uuid, search_id and stored columns, and — when you run the index check — entries listed more than once in search, entries missing from it, and records left behind by deleted entries.

instructions.title: File Format & Import Instructions
instructions.mergedRows: Multiple CSV rows sharing the same UUID or Chinese term are merged into one glossary entry with multiple translations.
instructions.stepChunks: Chunk display — the file is divided into chunks of {{chunkSize}} glossary terms (not rows). Each term may span several CSV rows when it has multiple translations.
instructions.stepReview: Review — the left column shows what is currently in the database; the right column shows the entry as it will be stored after the merge. Green cards are new entries; amber cards are updates. Within a card, each translation is tagged Kept, Updated or New.
instructions.stepImport: Import Chunk — click the button to write the current chunk to the database, then the next chunk is shown automatically.
instructions.conflictMatching: Rows with a UUID are matched to the existing record by primary key. Rows without a UUID are matched by Chinese term. New entries are created and indexed in Algolia automatically.
instructions.conflictMerge: When a match is found the entry's translations are merged, not replaced — translations already in the database are kept even if the file does not mention them, so an import file only needs to carry the terms it is adding. A translation is considered the same as a stored one when its EnglishTerm, SutraName and Volume all match; in that case the file wins and the stored sutra text is overwritten. Everything else is appended. Re-importing the same file therefore changes nothing.
instructions.conflictMetadata: Entry-level metadata (phonetic, author, CBETA frequency) is overwritten by the file when supplied; leaving a cell blank keeps the stored value. To remove a translation, edit the entry directly — an import cannot delete one.

replace.title: Replace Glossary
replace.description: Upload a CSV or XLSX file to replace the entire glossary. The first write clears all existing entries, then the file is imported in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms at a time.
replace.warning: Starting the import permanently deletes every existing glossary entry before writing the file. This cannot be undone — download a CSV backup first.
replace.confirmWipe: This permanently deletes all existing glossary entries before importing. Continue?
replace.uuidConflicts_one: {{count}} term carries more than one UUID in this file ({{terms}}). Each term can only be one entry, so the first UUID is kept and the others are discarded. Fix the file if those ids matter.
replace.uuidConflicts_other: {{count}} terms carry more than one UUID in this file ({{terms}}). Each term can only be one entry, so the first UUID is kept and the others are discarded. Fix the file if those ids matter.
replace.writing: Writing {{terms}} ({{rows}}). Upload a new file above to start over.

instructions.title: File Format & Replace Instructions
instructions.mergedRows: Multiple rows sharing the same UUID or Chinese term are merged into one glossary entry with multiple translations.
instructions.stepChunks: Chunk display — the file is divided into chunks of {{chunkSize}} glossary terms (not rows). Each term may span several rows when it has multiple translations.
instructions.stepReview: Review — each chunk lists the entries it will write. There is no side-by-side comparison, because the existing glossary is discarded rather than merged.
instructions.stepImport: Import Chunk — writes the current chunk and advances. The first write deletes every existing glossary entry before inserting.
instructions.existingWipe: Starting the import permanently deletes every existing glossary entry, then writes the file's entries as new records. There is no per-row matching or merging against current data — the file becomes the complete glossary. New entries are indexed in Algolia automatically.
instructions.existingPartial: The wipe happens as part of the first chunk's write, and the remaining chunks are separate requests. If you stop partway the glossary will contain only the chunks written so far, so download a CSV backup before you start.

errors.invalidFileType: Invalid file type. Please upload a CSV or XLSX file.
errors.noValidRows: No valid rows found. Ensure the file has a ChineseTerm column.
